If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to align with upward momentum bias.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward drift.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum carryover.

If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 1.0–2.0% for the next 5-day window to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, suppress forecast spikes in late horizon (20–30 days) to avoid overcorrection from momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% to early horizon (1–10 days) to prevent overoptimism.
